shifts.summary: Candidates reported the paper overall as easy to moderate. Reasoning was described as mostly easy with some analytical and puzzle questions. General awareness was moderate with a mix of current affairs and history topics. Quantitative section was the hardest, with timing pressure and advanced geometry and measurement problems. English was generally easy with vocabulary and rearrangement questions.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reported that reasoning was mostly easy, with many statement based questions and at least eight analytical questions. Some puzzle type questions were noted as tougher.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: General awareness was described as moderate. Questions included 2023 World Cup winner, awards, articles, Mughal history and economics.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant was the hardest section, with a 15‑minute limit for 25 questions. Topics ranged from advanced calculative one‑liners to geometry, measurement and proportion problems.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was reported as easy with vocabulary and rearrangement questions. Additional focus was on synonyms, idioms and phrasal verbs.

asked.q: Which address is different among the three address‑based questions?

observations: Overall difficulty was easy to moderate across most reports.
Quantitative section faced timing pressure and was rated hardest.
Reasoning difficulty varied, with some reports calling it easy and others moderate.
English questions were largely easy, focusing on vocabulary and rearrangement.
disagreements: Reasoning difficulty split: 1 report easy, 1 moderate, 1 easy to moderate.
Quant difficulty split: reports ranged from difficult to advanced to moderate to difficult.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 27 October 2026 was reported as easy to moderate overall, with most candidates describing the reasoning portion as mostly easy and the quantitative section as the hardest. English was generally easy, focusing on vocabulary and rearrangement questions, while general awareness covered a mix of current affairs and history. Unofficial figures suggest that between 20 and 78 candidates had good attempts, but these numbers are not confirmed by SSC. The SSC normalises scores across shifts, and shifts 2 and 3 have not yet produced usable analysis.
